meta.window: 2026-09-23T02:46Z to 2026-10-06T02:12Z (blocks 26037294..26130271, whole life of the collection, ~13 days)
meta.units: price_eth in ETH; wei_per_point = wei per whole score point (score_1e4/1e4); score points range 80..800
meta.note: the whole collection life is only ~13 days: 30d and 90d medians equal the whole-window median and are labelled as such

flat_vs_per_point_model_fit.note: each model uses the same day's median (flat: median price per credit; per point: median wei per point times score); lower error wins

regression_price_on_score.verdict: flat price per credit across scores 80..~700 (relative price within 1-3% of day median in every bucket, r2 ~0.5% pooled); a convex premium only appears above ~740 pts and is large above 790 (median ~2x, only ~1.4% of credits). buyers do NOT pay per point in the core of the distribution.

score_distribution_points.note: score = scoreOf(seedOf(id), timestampOf(id)) read on chain for all 122,154 ids (full census, not a sample)

movements_not_counted_as_sales.note: mints are all in the first day; every non-sale move with tx.value>0 or WETH in tx is flagged in the raw rows but not priced

listing_price_eth_now.note: nftForSale(id) read on chain at block 26130271 for every held id; all equal 1.2x the strategy's own purchase price. seaport listings by third parties are NOT derivable from logs (off chain order signatures)

purchases.note: strategy pays a flat tier price per credit regardless of score; tier steps look like 0.025/0.03/0.035/0.04 and fell to 0.01 after its eth ran out

arb_roundtrips_sell_then_buy_back_same_t.note: strategy sells a relisted credit at its 1.2x listing and the same tx sells it back at the (higher) current bid tier: a risk-free arb that drains the strategy

fee_model.note: verified on traces: hook takes ~10% of the eth notional (coin side on buys, eth side on sells) and forwards 80% to the strategy, 10% to each of two other recipients; strategy inflow reconciled from eth_getBalance every 300 blocks is 7.7% of notional after the first ~600 blocks, matching 8%
fee_model.launch_surcharge: the first ~600 blocks (~2h) carried a decaying launch fee: strategy inflow was 39.8% of notional right after launch (hook fee ~50%) falling to 8% by ~block +600; first 300 blocks: 915 eth volume, 322 eth to the strategy

concentration.note: matched share is volume that a trader both bought and sold; high values mean heavy round trip churn (market makers, bots, or wash)

buybacks.note: BoughtAndBurned events: the strategy spends its credit sale proceeds (~1:1) on buying and burning its coin

statements.note_on_weekly_rate: all 153 statements were composed in the first 4.1 days after the statements contract went live (2026/10/02 00:15 utc); weekly rates cannot be extrapolated, the run rate decays 119, 19, 9, 3, 3 per day

overprints.note: overprinted statements hold 80*(1+overprints) credits and rate up to 7.8x the base; creditsOf returns 160/240/320/640 for them

premium_over_parts.definition: ratio = statement sale price / estimated cost of its credits at the time of sale. flat cost = credits_count x trailing 24h median market credit price (eth); per point cost = rating points x trailing 24h median market wei per point. >1 premium, <1 discount

ratio_vs_per_point.note: noisy: per point cost scales with rating, but price does not (see regression)

sale_vs_actual_cost_basis.note: cost basis scaled to 80 credits from the priced ones; composers mostly bought credits near the launch price

auction_4x_to_1_2x_cost_feasibility.verdict: statements sold at a median 0.84x of their credits' market cost (a discount). 9 of 42 sales (21%) reached 1.2x, the maximum was 1.32x and none came near 4x. an auction that starts at 4x and floors at 1.2x of cost would clear only against the top ~20% of observed buyers and would not clear at 4x at all
auction_4x_to_1_2x_cost_feasibility.caveat: only 42 priced statement sales exist; cost defined with trailing market credit price, not what the builder actually paid

strategy_feed.note: one bot (0xc8bd1dca...) delivered 55% of everything the strategy bought: single actor dominance. the same address family mostly sweeps the lowest seaport listings

fwa_hub.note: fwa hub 0x958c: depositors escrow a credit with eth backing 0.025 to 0.032 (a flat band, not score based); accepted bids pay that same flat band (gross = payout + 10% fee), even when the open market is far below it

pool.note: 71% of CREDITSTR pool volume is matched buy and sell volume by the same tx sender: heavy round trip churn; top 10 senders are only 16% so no single wash actor, but more than half of volume is two sided churn (bots, arb, market making)

wash_and_dominance.verdict: no single wallet dominates organic market sales (top buyer ~3% of eth, top10 buyers ~14% of count); concentration risk is in (a) one searcher bot feeding 55% of strategy purchases, (b) 27% of sales rows sit in repeat pairs of >=5 trades (sweeper bots buying a dumper's whole stack) which is ordinary sweeping but should be treated as one actor, (c) CreditStrategy holds 12% of all live credits, (d) 71% pool churn. clear self-trades (buyer==seller) are ~0.

bid_design.formula: hours = ln(target/4e12)/ln(1.01); 1%/h compounding = x1.27/day, x5.3/week, x14 per 2 weeks
bid_design.per_point_pricing_by_sellers: not observed: fills are flat per credit between 80 and ~700 points; the only score premium is at >=740 points
bid_design.note: the bid only wins credits whose flat ask is below bid_per_point x score. a per point bid therefore clears the highest score credits first and the lowest score credits last (adverse for the bidder: it overpays high score credits relative to their flat ask)
